nodes.directText: Snapshot testing and assertion testing serve different purposes in test automation:
nodes.subtreeText: Snapshot testing and assertion testing serve different purposes in test automation:

nodes.accessibleName: Assertion testing Direct link to Assertion testing

nodes.directText: Assertion testing is a targeted approach where you assert specific values or conditions about elements or components. For instance, with Playwright, verifies that an element contains the expected text, and confirms that an input field has t
nodes.subtreeText: Assertion testing is a targeted approach where you assert specific values or conditions about elements or components. For instance, with Playwright, expect(locator).toHaveText() verifies that an element contains the expected text, and expect(locator).toHaveValue() confirms that an input field has the expected value. Assertion tests are specific and generally check the current state of an element or property against an expected, predefined state. They work well for predictable, single-value check

Clarity : The intent of the test is explicit and easy to understand. Specificity : Tests focus on particular aspects of functionality, making them more robust against unrelated changes. Debugging : Failures provide targeted feedback, pointing directly to the problematic aspect.

nodes.accessibleName: Snapshot testing Direct link to Snapshot testing

nodes.directText: Snapshot testing captures a “snapshot” or representation of the entire state of an element, component, or data at a given moment, which is then saved for future comparisons. When re-running tests, the current state is compared to the snapsh
nodes.subtreeText: Snapshot testing captures a “snapshot” or representation of the entire state of an element, component, or data at a given moment, which is then saved for future comparisons. When re-running tests, the current state is compared to the snapshot, and if there are differences, the test fails. This approach is especially useful for complex or dynamic structures, where manually asserting each detail would be too time-consuming. Snapshot testing is broader and more holistic than assertion testing, allo

Simplifies complex outputs : For example, testing a UI component's rendered output can be tedious with traditional assertions. Snapshots capture the entire output for easy comparison. Quick Feedback loop : Developers can easily spot unintended changes in the output. Encourages consistency : Helps maintain consistent output as code evolves.

Granularity : Large snapshots may be hard to interpret when differences arise, especially if minor changes affect large portions of the output. Suitability : Not ideal for highly dynamic content where outputs change frequently or unpredictably.

nodes.accessibleName: Aria snapshots Direct link to Aria snapshots

nodes.directText: In Playwright, aria snapshots provide a YAML representation of the accessibility tree of a page. These snapshots can be stored and compared later to verify if the page structure remains consistent or meets defined expectations.
nodes.subtreeText: In Playwright, aria snapshots provide a YAML representation of the accessibility tree of a page. These snapshots can be stored and compared later to verify if the page structure remains consistent or meets defined expectations.

nodes.directText: The YAML format describes the hierarchical structure of accessible elements on the page, detailing , , , and . The structure follows a tree-like syntax, where each node represents an accessible element, and indentation indicates nested elem
nodes.subtreeText: The YAML format describes the hierarchical structure of accessible elements on the page, detailing roles , attributes , values , and text content . The structure follows a tree-like syntax, where each node represents an accessible element, and indentation indicates nested elements.

nodes.directText: Each accessible element in the tree is represented as a YAML node:
nodes.subtreeText: Each accessible element in the tree is represented as a YAML node:

role : Specifies the ARIA or HTML role of the element (e.g., heading , list , listitem , button ). "name" : Accessible name of the element. Quoted strings indicate exact values, /patterns/ are used for regular expression. [attribute=value] : Attributes and values, in square brackets, represent specific ARIA attributes, such as checked , disabled , expanded , invalid , level , pressed , or selected .

nodes.accessibleName: Snapshot matching Direct link to Snapshot matching

nodes.directText: The assertion method in Playwright compares the accessible structure of the page with a predefined aria snapshot template, helping validate the page's state against testing requirements. You can also use to match a specific part of the page
nodes.subtreeText: The expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot() assertion method in Playwright compares the accessible structure of the page with a predefined aria snapshot template, helping validate the page's state against testing requirements. You can also use expect(locator).toMatchAriaSnapshot() to match a specific part of the page.

nodes.directText: You can match it using the following snapshot template:
nodes.subtreeText: You can match it using the following snapshot template:

nodes.directText: When matching, the snapshot template is compared to the current accessibility tree of the page:
nodes.subtreeText: When matching, the snapshot template is compared to the current accessibility tree of the page:

If the tree structure matches the template, the test passes; otherwise, it fails, indicating a mismatch between expected and actual accessibility states. The comparison is case-sensitive and collapses whitespace, so indentation and line breaks are ignored. The comparison is order-sensitive, meaning the order of elements in the snapshot template must match the order in the page's accessibility tree.

nodes.directText: You can perform partial matches on nodes by omitting attributes or accessible names, enabling verification of specific parts of the accessibility tree without requiring exact matches. This flexibility is helpful for dynamic or irrelevant at
nodes.subtreeText: You can perform partial matches on nodes by omitting attributes or accessible names, enabling verification of specific parts of the accessibility tree without requiring exact matches. This flexibility is helpful for dynamic or irrelevant attributes.

nodes.directText: In this example, the button role is matched, but the accessible name ("Submit") is not specified, allowing the test to pass regardless of the button's label.

nodes.directText: For elements with ARIA attributes like or , omitting these attributes allows partial matching, focusing solely on role and hierarchy.

nodes.directText: In this partial match, the attribute is ignored, so the test will pass regardless of the checkbox state.

nodes.directText: When using the Playwright test runner ( ), you can automatically update snapshots with the flag, for short.
nodes.subtreeText: When using the Playwright test runner ( @playwright/test ), you can automatically update snapshots with the --update-snapshots flag, -u for short.

nodes.directText: Running tests with the flag will update snapshots that did not match. Matching snapshots will not be updated.
nodes.subtreeText: Running tests with the --update-snapshots flag will update snapshots that did not match. Matching snapshots will not be updated.

nodes.directText: Updating snapshots is useful when application structure changes require new snapshots as a baseline. Note that Playwright will wait for the maximum expect timeout specified in the test runner configuration to ensure the page is settled befo
nodes.subtreeText: Updating snapshots is useful when application structure changes require new snapshots as a baseline. Note that Playwright will wait for the maximum expect timeout specified in the test runner configuration to ensure the page is settled before taking the snapshot. It might be necessary to adjust the --timeout if the test hits the timeout while generating snapshots.

nodes.directText: When updating snapshots, Playwright creates patch files that capture differences. These patch files can be reviewed, applied, and committed to source control, allowing teams to track structural changes over time and ensure updates are consi
nodes.subtreeText: When updating snapshots, Playwright creates patch files that capture differences. These patch files can be reviewed, applied, and committed to source control, allowing teams to track structural changes over time and ensure updates are consistent with application requirements.

nodes.directText: The way source code is updated can be changed using the flag. There are several options available:
nodes.subtreeText: The way source code is updated can be changed using the --update-source-method flag. There are several options available:

"patch" (default): Generates a unified diff file that can be applied to the source code using git apply . "3way" : Generates merge conflict markers in your source code, allowing you to choose whether to accept changes. "overwrite" : Overwrites the source code with the new snapshot values.
